question: Revenue is 8% higher each year. What will it be after 4 years?

mutation.description: applies growth for one too few periods
uses a decrease multiplier instead of a growth multiplier
applies the rate to the original value only
matches the formula and every calculation step
uses a nearby value that does not follow the stated calculation

explanation: Read the values from the chart and apply the stated operation. Formula: initial × (1 + rate ÷ 100)^years. Growth factor: 1 + rate ÷ 100; substitute 1 + 8 ÷ 100 = 1.08 factor; exact. After year 1: previous value × growth factor; substitute 300.00 × 1.080 = 324 thousand EUR; rounded to 2 decimal places. After year 2: previous value × growth factor; substitute 324.00 × 1.080 = 349.92 thousand EUR; rounded to 2 decimal places. After year 3: previous value × growth factor; substitute 349.92 × 1.080 = 377.91 thousand EUR; rounded to 2 decimal places. After year 4: previous value × growth factor; substitute 377.91 × 1.080 = 408.15 thousand EUR; rounded to 2 decimal places. Final result: 408.15 thousand EUR (rounded to 2 decimal places where needed). Option D is correct. Visual shortcut: Follow the line trend, then apply the same multiplier for each additional year. Each distractor records the specific calculation mistake it makes.
